import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

The target run is unambiguous: `research.0s.image` is the image agent, and its saved response explicitly ended with “currently uncommitted.” The launch prompt had `#gh:gh_sase-org__sase` but no explicit rollover xprompt, so I’m tracing whether the defect is in launch metadata, finalizer eligibility, dirty-repository discovery, or the runtime’s second-turn scheduling before choosing the fix scope.

The finalizer then scanned the correctly recorded workspace clone, found it clean, and reported `reason: no_changes`. I’m now testing the intended safety boundary: whether the fix should detect and fail on mutations to the primary clone, redirect path resolution earlier, or both—without ever treating shared primary-checkout dirt as ordinary agent-owned work.

The historical design confirms that scanning shared primaries as normal commit targets was intentionally removed when linked repositories became host-workspace scoped; restoring that behavior would let a finalizer commit another process’s work. The safe fix therefore needs attribution plus remediation, not a blanket “scan every primary and commit it.” I’m checking the earlier safety plan and current generated-skill contract before locking the tale plan.

I’ve chosen a medium tale: the root cause and correction are bounded enough for one implementation agent, but the change crosses baseline capture, dirty-repo classification, prompt safety, generated guidance, and regression coverage. The plan will preserve isolation by watching only primary counterparts of repositories actually opened by the run, and it will require a launch-time baseline before treating their later dirt as attributable—so pre-existing shared work is never swept into a commit prompt.

The explanatory validation did its job: the tale schema requires `title` and `goal` in frontmatter in addition to tier and size. I’m applying only those schema fields, then performing the required clean revalidation without `--explain`.

The medium tale now passes revalidation with zero warnings. Its fix is deliberately two-layered: stronger path discipline prevents the stale-path mistake, while baseline-attributed finalizer detection catches it if guidance is ignored. I’m submitting it through `sase plan propose` now; this intentionally hands the work to the approval gate and approved implementation continuation before any implementation file is changed.
